FEATURE GUIDE

Recognize explicit half-day events

Read morning-off and afternoon-off titles while keeping your manual workday choice in control.

Mac 1.5.15 build31

OverviewHow to useExampleSupport and limitsRelated features

Overview

Leave recognition is an optional module that reads explicit morning or afternoon half-day titles from a connected event source. It does not infer half days from general annual-leave events or your remaining leave balance.

A manually chosen workday mode takes priority over automatic recognition. You can choose today’s mode without a calendar connection.

How to use

  1. Install and enable leave recognition in Settings → Plugin management.
  2. Enable automatic half-day recognition in the module’s settings.
  3. Under Feature connections, choose Calendar or DaouOffice as the half-day source. Install, enable and connect that source too.
  4. Check the event titles it can access. If shared events may be mistaken for yours, choose today’s mode manually or disable recognition.

Example

“Morning half day”

A “Morning half day” or “Half day AM” title selects the afternoon arrival mode. A default example is arrival at 13:00 and scheduled departure at 17:00.

“Afternoon half day”

An “Afternoon half day” or “Half day PM” title selects the morning arrival mode. A default example is arrival at 09:00 and scheduled departure at 13:00.

Annual leave or a balance

Neither selects a morning or afternoon half day by itself. Choose the appropriate mode manually.

Half days use four hours without a break. The last-Friday two-hour reduction is not added again.

Support and limits

This guide covers the optional module in Mac 1.5.15 build31. Windows 1.5.13 has no corresponding plugin settings. The developer is HappyLulu contributors.

Accessible shared events may be interpreted as yours. Check ownership and use a manual mode when needed. DaouOffice event coverage is limited to the current month.

This does not submit leave requests, calculate annual-leave balances, classify general leave or reconstruct past arrivals. Disabling the module retains saved source choices; an explicit “Not connected” choice also stays unchanged.
